newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Goldfields in WA native title talks.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Goldfields in WA native title talks.

text.p: Goldfields Ltd said on Wednesday it is in negotiations with Aboriginal leaders over native title claims on its South Talbot gold deposit in Western Australia.
Peter Cassidy, managing director of Goldfields, said talks with three separate claimant groups were in the "embryonic stage."
He said he expected a fourth claim to be lodged shortly.

Goldfields is hoping to begin mine stripping work at South Talbot in February in order to supply higher grade ore to its Paddington mine operation, which is being burdened by high operating costs, Cassidy said.
Failure to reach an agreement with the tribes would see the claims go before the Native Title Tribunal, which could delay the mine's development by about five months, Cassidy said.

However, the delay would not have much impact in the 1996/97 fiscal year to June 30 since early work at South Talbot would focus on depleting a top layer of lower-grade ore, Cassidy said. "The benefit grade-wise comes in the 1997/98 and 1998/99 years," he said.
Cash costs averaged US$350 an ounce at Paddington in 1995/96, Cassidy said.
Goldfields earlier on Wednesday reported a net profit of A$11.1 million for its first year of operation.
For 1996/97 the company said it expectes to post a net profit in the range of A$20 million to $25 million.
Cassidy said South Talbot has a current resource of about 360,000 ounces.
A further 80,000 ounces is contained in the Keith Kilkenny joint venture, 100 km north east of Kalgoorlie, Cassidy said.
"What we're looking for is additional resources to try and put together a project of five years's duration at 100,000 ounces a year production, Cassidy said.
"To do that, we'd probably need something like 700,000 or 800,000 ounces in resources," he said.
